Subject: Azure PO — invoice routing & reseller passthrough

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked for clarity on how invoicing will work once we go live under the Azure private offer. Two specific asks: 1) can Redwood invoice Clearwave directly for the contracted usage while Enterprise Cloud Partners (our reseller) receives a separate reseller commission? 2) What evidence do we need to provide to Azure/Marketplace to validate the reseller pass-through so there are no listing or payout delays?

We're working to finalize the PO this week and would like to include invoice routing language and an expected timetable for reseller credits. I attached the early PO draft for reference (Clearwave_AZ_PO_Draft.pdf).

Appreciate a quick rundown so we can close on the PO.

Best,

Clearwave Health

Alex — thanks for the clear asks and for the draft PO. Quick answers up front: yes, we can have Redwood invoice Clearwave directly for usage under the private offer, and we can support a separate reseller commission flow to Enterprise Cloud Partners. However, Azure Marketplace requires specific invoice routing and reseller evidence before the reseller is eligible for pass-through credits.

To move fast, can you confirm two things:
- The reseller partner legal name and billing contact (I see Lisa on cc but need the invoice address you expect the partner to bill to).
- Whether the reseller will accept a net-back calculation (we invoice gross, then a partner contract invoices the reseller uplift), or if you prefer Redwood to invoice net of the reseller commission.

Once confirmed, I'll loop in Jordan (deal ops) and Irene (marketplace ops) to surface the exact evidence list and timeline. We can generally close the PO and add a clause that routing will follow the attached invoice matrix — final routing contingent on evidence submission to Azure.

Tentative next steps:
- Confirm reseller billing details (you)
- Redwood to provide invoice routing matrix + evidence checklist (we)
- Clearwave to submit partner authorization docs to Azure (you)

I'll attach a quick matrix for how we've handled similar Azure private offers.

—Marissa

Marissa / Jordan — we can support the flow but need the following to be submitted before any reseller credits are processed by Azure marketplace:

Required items (minimum):
- Reseller legal entity name and tax ID (for marketplace registration).
- Signed reseller acknowledgement or addendum (one-page) confirming commission % and routing.
- Partner Marketplace ID (the reseller must be registered in Azure Marketplace and tied to the private offer).
- Example reseller invoice (PDF) showing how they will bill/credit the customer or passthrough.
- Proof of authorized relationship (MSA excerpt or partner letterhead) to show reseller entitlement.

Mechanics we recommend:
- Redwood issues primary invoice to Clearwave for the private-offer usage (monthly).
- Enterprise Cloud Partners issues a separate invoice to Clearwave for their services/marketplace uplift. Azure will validate partner passthrough via the Partner Marketplace ID and the reseller evidence above; payouts to the reseller usually trail first invoice by one billing cycle if evidence is complete.

Attached: invoice-routing-matrix.xlsx (contains the exact line items we put into the PO language and examples of routing clauses). Also consolidated a zipped folder (reseller-evidence.zip) with templates we ask partners to use.

Risk notes: if partner registration or evidence is incomplete, Azure will hold reseller payout until validation is done — customer may request Redwood to net-down the partner share on our invoice as a workaround, but that puts Redwood on the hook for the uplift and changes revenue recognition. We should avoid that if possible.

If you want, I can draft PO language for the routing and an evidence checklist to include as an appendix.

—Irene
Marketplace Ops Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: invoice-routing-matrix.xlsx, reseller-evidence.zip

Alex / Lisa — thanks for the quick responses. Per Irene's checklist, here's the agreed approach so we can finalize the PO and target a Jan 1, 2028 go-live:

Agreed routing and timing:
- Redwood will invoice Clearwave directly for private-offer usage on a monthly cadence.
- Enterprise Cloud Partners will receive reseller payouts via Azure Marketplace after partner validation. Payouts typically begin the billing cycle following validation (expected 30–60 days after first invoice).
- If Clearwave prefers reseller credits to appear on month-one, Enterprise can instead provide a partner credit memo to the customer and Redwood will invoice net-of-credit; that requires Redwood to own the uplift and will impact revenue accounting (we prefer the marketplace pass-through).

Action items:
